text:
Maya Chen: quick heads-up — I just ran a targeted surge sim against eu-west (region eu-west-1) and hit an unexpected egress/network constraint before GPUs saturated. results look like: tokens/sec dropped ~18% at peak, p99 generation jumped to ~420ms, concurrent handled requests plateaued ~22k even though GPU util was ~60%.

Raj Patel: can you paste the sim config? is this the real user-mix or a synthetic high-embed workload?

Maya Chen: synthetic mix but weighted to match Jan-Dec seasonality curve (more long-chat sessions). command used: 
```
sim-run --region eu-west-1 --model mix:a100-32g --qps 24000 --duration 30m --session-length mean=120 tokens mean_resp=180
```
Key point: egress from the inference nodes hit the VPC NAT egress limit — packets queued at the node and kv-cache fetch latency increased. GPU-side metrics show stalls waiting on 1-3ms network callbacks which cascaded to token generation.

Lin Zhao: so this is a network egress throughput cap rather than pure compute. what was the measured node-level NIC utilization?

Maya Chen: NIC peaked at ~95% on 10Gb instances; CPU on host low, GPU mem and SM occupancy not near max. topology shows many small responses with lots of prefix cache churn (many short requests with embeddings + function calls).

Amir Hussein: rough cost impact if we scale NIC to 25Gb (upgrade flavor) across the pool? how many extra GPU hours would we burn because of faster tail handling?

Maya Chen: estimated: current warm-up/waste adds ~12% extra GPU-hours for eu-west under peak. fixing egress (so tokens/sec recovers) would reduce that back to baseline — net saving ~+0.12 * weekly_gpu_hours. But upgrading instance nets adds ~35% infra cost on those nodes; we need to compare against wasted GPU-hours and customer SLA exposure.

Raj Patel: could we mitigate without a full instance type change? ideas: 1) route a % of long sessions to eu-central/uk which has spare egress, 2) increase batching window slightly to reduce per-request packets, 3) move pre/post token payload handling to edge LB to reduce egress size.

Maya Chen: yes. ran a quick reroute sim (30% diverted to eu-central) — tail p99 improved to ~260ms, tokens/sec to ~95% of target. downside: cross-region routing increases cost and may slightly raise median latency for those users.

Sophie (oncall): any risk to customers during normal traffic tomorrow morning? we have scheduled weekly rollout at 08:00 UTC; if the pattern holds we could see degraded p99 for ~3–4 hours unless mitigated.

Lin Zhao: short-term actions I suggest: 
- apply a routing policy to keep long sessions under dedicated eu-central pool (can use route weight 0.3)
- increase batching buffer from 8ms -> 12ms for eu-west pool (trade slightly higher median latency for 10% less egress)
- open an infra ticket to test a 25Gb flavor in a canary zone

Maya Chen: I'll open the ticket and run a canary today. ticket link: https://jira.redwood.internal/browse/INFRA-8271

Amir Hussein: for cost modeling, can you export the sim run csv? I'll overlay on reserved vs on-demand cost curves and share a short calc.

Maya Chen: exporting now. sample snip from sim CSV (rows truncated):
```
ts,region,node,concurrent,tokens_sec,p99_ms,nic_util,gpu_util
1978765400,eu-west-1,node-17,21500,120k,420,95,60
1978765410,eu-west-1,node-18,22000,118k,435,96,62
1978765420,eu-central-1,node-3,7200,40k,160,30,55
```

Raj Patel: nice. Amir — if we decide routing+batching fixes most pain, can we make that a temporary policy for the seasonal window (Nov–Jan) and only upgrade instances if traffic still fails tests?

Amir Hussein: yes that's the plan. I'll model the break-even point: extra infra cost vs reduced wasted GPU-hours and SLA penalty risk.

Sophie (oncall): FYI I'll add an incident channel watch for tomorrow 07:30–11:30 UTC and will be ready to flip routing weights if noise spikes.

Maya Chen: plan of record: 1) apply routing 30% long-sessions -> eu-central canary at 06:30 UTC, 2) bump batching window for eu-west to 12ms, 3) run canary with 25Gb flavor nodes in zone-a to validate net improvement, 4) Amir to share cost spreadsheet by EOD. tagging @OpsBot to schedule the canary job.

OpsBot: Canary job scheduled: sim-canary-1978765432 at 06:30 UTC. Results will be posted to #eng-infra/canary-results.

Lin Zhao: small note — make sure the routing policy respects data residency flags for EU-regulated tenants; filter them out of cross-region diverts.

Maya Chen: already added a tenant filter to the policy.

Raj Patel: thanks — once Amir's cost calc is in we'll decide on long-term (reserved instance upsell vs routing + caching improvements).

Amir Hussein: uploaded the quick calc: https://drive.redwood.internal/drive/folders/infra/eu_egress_cost_calc.xlsx — early read: if peak > 80% sustained for >4h/day across week we should prefer instance upgrade, otherwise routing + batching wins.

Maya Chen: ok locking this thread into the follow-up doc (INFRA-8271) and will post a short summary to the morning all-hands if canary looks good. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Sophie (oncall): ack :+1:

Raj Patel: thanks team.
